items.title: Process vs thread
items.overview: A process has isolated address space and OS resources; threads share address space within a process. Context switch cost and communication patterns differ.
selfCheckQuestions: Why is inter-process communication slower than sharing memory between threads?
What happens to threads when a process exits?
How does Go's goroutine model relate to OS threads?
checklist: Define process and thread in one sentence each
Explain why races are easier with shared memory
items.whyGoogle: Systems fundamentals underpin concurrency and performance discussions in loops.

items.title: User space vs kernel space
items.overview: Syscalls transition to kernel mode for privileged work (I/O, scheduling). Frequent syscalls can dominate latency.
selfCheckQuestions: What triggers a context switch besides time slices?
Why can excessive small reads be slow on files?
What role does the page table play in isolation?
items.youtubeSearch: user mode kernel mode syscall explained
items.whyGoogle: Explains why batching and async I/O matter at scale.

items.title: Virtual memory and paging
items.overview: Virtual addresses map to physical frames via page tables. Demand paging and TLB misses affect performance; swapping causes thrashing.
selfCheckQuestions: What is a page fault and when is it benign?
How does virtual memory enable overcommit?
What is locality of reference?
checklist: Draw virtual to physical mapping verbally
items.whyGoogle: Memory-heavy services and GC tuning connect to this mental model.

items.title: CPU scheduling basics
items.overview: Schedulers pick runnable tasks using policies (CFS on Linux). CPU-bound vs I/O-bound workloads need different parallelism.
selfCheckQuestions: What is preemptive scheduling?
Why might more threads hurt CPU-bound work?
How do niceness and cgroups relate to priority?
checklist: Contrast FCFS vs priority at concept level
Relate GOMAXPROCS to physical cores pragmatically
items.whyGoogle: Capacity planning and tail latency stories use scheduling vocabulary.

items.title: Locks, mutexes, and deadlocks
items.overview: Mutual exclusion prevents races. Deadlock needs four conditions; prevention via ordering, timeouts, or lock-free structures.
selfCheckQuestions: State the four Coffman conditions for deadlock.
How does lock ordering prevent deadlock?
What is livelock?
checklist: Give a deadlock example with two locks
Connect to Go mutex best practices
items.whyGoogle: Distributed and multithreaded Google systems fail in subtle lock-related ways.

items.title: Memory hierarchy and caching
items.overview: Registers, L1/L2/L3, RAM, disk—latency jumps by orders of magnitude. Cache-friendly access patterns improve throughput.
selfCheckQuestions: Why does sequential array scan beat linked list traversal often?
What is false sharing?
How does cache line size affect concurrent counters?
items.whyGoogle: Performance interviews reference cache even for high-level engineers.

items.title: File systems and durability
items.overview: Files are metadata + blocks. fsync and journal modes trade durability for speed. Crash consistency is hard.
selfCheckQuestions: What does fsync guarantee after success?
Difference between page cache and disk?
Why is append-only log common for durability?
checklist: Name one consistency scenario after power loss
items.whyGoogle: Storage design questions assume OS durability basics.

items.title: B-tree and hash indexes
items.overview: B-trees support range scans and ordered indexes; hash indexes excel at point lookups. Composite indexes follow left-prefix rule.
selfCheckQuestions: When does a query use a covering index?
Why can't you skip the leftmost column in a composite index?
Compare index selectivity.
items.whyGoogle: SQL performance tuning is common in backend onsite topics.

items.title: ACID properties
items.overview: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability—transactions bundle work with guarantees enforced by the engine.
selfCheckQuestions: Which ACID property does WAL primarily support?
Is consistency only the database's job?
Give an example violating atomicity.
checklist: Define each letter with an example
items.whyGoogle: Financial and ads systems require crisp transaction language.

items.title: Isolation levels and anomalies
items.overview: Read committed, repeatable read, serializable—each prevents some of dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom read.
selfCheckQuestions: Which anomaly does SELECT FOR UPDATE address?
What is snapshot isolation?
Why might you accept read committed?
items.whyGoogle: Correctness under concurrency is a Google bar for data engineers.

items.title: SQL joins and query plans
items.overview: Inner, left, semi joins combine relations. Optimizer picks nested loop, hash join, merge join based on stats and indexes.
selfCheckQuestions: When is hash join preferred?
What does EXPLAIN ANALYZE show you?
Difference between WHERE and ON in LEFT JOIN?
checklist: Write join for many-to-many via bridge table
items.youtubeSearch: SQL joins hash merge nested loop
items.whyGoogle: Debugging slow queries appears in practical interviews.

items.title: Normalization vs denormalization
items.overview: Normal forms reduce redundancy; denormalization speeds reads at update anomaly cost. OLTP vs OLAP bias differs.
selfCheckQuestions: Give an example of update anomaly in unnormalized data.
When is star schema appropriate?
How do materialized views fit?
checklist: Balance with read QPS in design
items.whyGoogle: Schema design trade-offs surface in system design deep dives.

items.title: Replication and leader-follower
items.overview: Primary handles writes; replicas serve reads with lag. Failover promotes new leader; split-brain requires fencing.
selfCheckQuestions: What is replication lag and user-visible symptom?
Sync vs async replication trade-off?
How does quorum relate to writes?
items.whyGoogle: Google-scale storage discussions assume replication fluency.

items.title: Sharding and partitioning
items.overview: Horizontal split by shard key; hotspots if skewed. Resharding and cross-shard queries are operational pain.
selfCheckQuestions: What makes a good shard key?
How do you handle range vs hash sharding?
What is a scatter-gather query cost?
items.whyGoogle: Large Google products are sharded by default mentally.

items.title: CAP and PACELC intuition
items.overview: Under partition, choose consistency or availability for writes. PACELC extends trade-offs when network is normal.
selfCheckQuestions: Is CAP a theorem you optimize away?
Where does Spanner sit in practice?
Eventual consistency user example?
checklist: Give CP vs AP example systems
Avoid absolutist CAP slogans in interviews
items.whyGoogle: Design interviews expect nuanced CAP, not memes.

items.title: SOLID principles overview
items.overview: SRP, OCP, LSP, ISP, DIP guide maintainable OO. In Go, interfaces and small packages echo these ideas.
selfCheckQuestions: Which SOLID principle do interfaces in Go emphasize most?
Give a violation of Liskov substitution.
How does DI relate to DIP?
checklist: Name each SOLID letter and one line meaning
Map SRP to a microservice boundary
items.whyGoogle: OO design still appears in LLD and code review scenarios.

items.title: Polymorphism and dynamic dispatch
items.overview: Single interface, many implementations. Virtual methods enable substitution; overuse hides performance costs.
selfCheckQuestions: Compile-time vs runtime polymorphism examples?
How does Go achieve polymorphism without inheritance?
When is switch on type an anti-pattern?
items.whyGoogle: Clean abstractions matter in million-line codebases.

items.title: Composition over inheritance
items.overview: Build behavior by combining types rather than deep hierarchies. Reduces fragile base class problems.
selfCheckQuestions: Why can deep inheritance hurt testing?
How does embedding in Go relate?
Example of favoring has-a over is-a?
checklist: Draw composition diagram for a feature
items.whyGoogle: Google style guides discourage heavy inheritance trees.

items.title: Encapsulation and invariants
items.overview: Hide representation; enforce invariants through constructors and methods. Invalid states should be unrepresentable when possible.
selfCheckQuestions: Why expose getters instead of public fields sometimes?
What is an invariant for a BankAccount?
How do builders help complex objects?
items.whyGoogle: Interview LLD prompts test whether types protect rules.

items.title: Design patterns: strategy and factory
items.overview: Strategy swaps algorithms; factory hides construction. Use when variation points are real—not speculatively.
selfCheckQuestions: When is a factory overkill?
Strategy vs template method?
Map strategy to Go interfaces.
items.whyGoogle: LLD rounds ask for extensible designs without over-engineering.

items.title: Paging vs segmentation (historical context)
items.overview: Paging fixed-size frames dominate; segmentation logical but fragmented. Modern OSes combine concepts via virtual memory.
selfCheckQuestions: What problem does paging solve vs segmentation?
What is internal fragmentation in pages?
Where do TLB misses fit?
items.whyGoogle: Shows academic OS knowledge applied succinctly.

items.title: Thrashing and working set
items.overview: When processes exceed RAM, excessive paging drops throughput. Working set model guides provisioning.
selfCheckQuestions: Symptoms of thrashing in metrics?
How does swap affect tail latency?
Relation to OOM killer?
items.whyGoogle: SRE-minded answers reference real observability.

items.title: Write-ahead logging (WAL)
items.overview: Log changes before applying to pages—enables crash recovery and replication. Checkpointing bounds recovery time.
selfCheckQuestions: Why log before data page update?
What does checkpoint do?
How does WAL relate to Postgres?
items.whyGoogle: Storage interviews love WAL for correctness stories.

items.title: Optimistic vs pessimistic locking
items.overview: Pessimistic locks rows upfront; optimistic checks version at commit. Optimistic wins low contention; retries under conflict.
selfCheckQuestions: What column supports optimistic locking?
When does pessimistic lock cause deadlocks?
HTTP If-Match analogy?
items.whyGoogle: Concurrency control choices appear in LLD and SQL deep dives.

items.title: Aggregate queries and GROUP BY
items.overview: Aggregates summarize rows; HAVING filters groups. Indexes may not help heavy aggregates without precomputation.
selfCheckQuestions: WHERE vs HAVING difference?
When materialized view helps?
Count(*) vs count(column)?
checklist: Write GROUP BY with HAVING example
items.whyGoogle: Analytics-flavored SQL shows up in practical screens.

items.title: Observer and pub-sub (conceptual)
items.overview: Publishers notify subscribers decoupled in time. Foundation for event-driven architectures and UI patterns.
selfCheckQuestions: Back-pressure problem in pub-sub?
How is this not the same as message queue?
Memory leak with forgotten subscribers?
items.whyGoogle: Event-driven systems are ubiquitous at Google.

items.title: Abstraction vs encapsulation
items.overview: Abstraction simplifies via models; encapsulation hides details. Both reduce cognitive load but address different axes.
selfCheckQuestions: API as abstraction example?
Can you have encapsulation without OO classes?
Leak of abstraction example?
items.whyGoogle: Clarifies design vocabulary under interview pressure.

items.title: Mutex vs semaphore
items.overview: Mutex binary lock for critical section; semaphore counts resources allowing N concurrent holders.
selfCheckQuestions: Can a semaphore act like mutex?
Priority inversion problem?
Go does not expose semaphores—what instead?
items.whyGoogle: Synchronization vocabulary crosses OS and Go interviews.

items.title: Secondary indexes and write amplification
items.overview: Each index updates on write—more indexes, higher write cost. Choose indexes from query patterns.
selfCheckQuestions: Partial index use case?
Unique index enforcement cost?
When composite index replaces two singles?
items.whyGoogle: Production DB tuning is a credibility signal.

items.title: Connection pooling
items.overview: Pools reuse TCP+auth sessions to DB. Size pool from concurrency and DB max_connections—not unbounded goroutines.
selfCheckQuestions: Symptom of pool too small?
Why is one connection per request bad?
Prepared statements and pooling?
items.whyGoogle: Backend onsite expects pool awareness with Go sql.

items.title: Template method pattern
items.overview: Skeleton algorithm in base type; subclasses override steps. Alternative: composition with injected functions in Go.
selfCheckQuestions: Downside of inheritance-based template?
Go equivalent with function parameters?
When hooks become fragile?
checklist: Prefer hooks over deep override trees
items.whyGoogle: LLD discussions compare patterns to idiomatic Go.

items.title: Copy-on-write and fork
items.overview: fork copies address space lazily via COW pages. Understanding COW helps with memory accounting and container images.
selfCheckQuestions: What breaks COW sharing?
Relation to Go GC heap?
Why is fork less central on Windows?
items.youtubeSearch: copy on write fork operating system
items.whyGoogle: Demonstrates depth beyond application-layer trivia.

items.title: Idempotency keys in data systems
items.overview: Retries duplicate requests; idempotent operations or dedup keys prevent double effects. Store key with unique constraint.
selfCheckQuestions: PUT vs POST idempotency HTTP tie-in?
How long to retain idempotency keys?
Exactly-once illusion components?
items.whyGoogle: Google APIs emphasize safe retries at scale.

items.title: Star schema for analytics
items.overview: Fact table surrounded by dimension tables—optimized for aggregations in warehouses, not OLTP updates.
selfCheckQuestions: Why denormalize dimensions?
Slowly changing dimension problem?
Columnar storage benefit?
items.whyGoogle: Ads and analytics context at Google references star schemas.

items.title: Interface segregation in practice
items.overview: Clients should not depend on methods they do not use—split fat interfaces into role-specific ones.
selfCheckQuestions: Fat interface smell in standard library counterexample?
How small should Go interfaces be?
Testing benefit of ISP?
checklist: Refactor one fat interface on paper
Relate ISP to micro API surfaces
items.whyGoogle: Aligns with Google Go readability and testability norms.
